title: one record, wherever it is held
line: John Y Davidson's 1946 Kentucky death certificate, held four ways: FamilySearch's page of it (the death as 1946), the certificate's image read by the model (the 11th, state file 14205), FamilySearch's index entry (the 11th) and the state index's own line (certificate 14205 of 1946). The page, the image and the index entry were archived under the file's one citation and the line gives the certificate's number: one record. The owner decides the page once; the image's reading, the index entry and the line take that decision with no card of their own; the certificate's own day, stated first-hand on the image, settles the file's 10th; the screen and the written conclusion cite the record once with its copies beneath it; and the owner's word that the line is another record gives back what the decision carried to it, the line a card again that the rule leaves to the owner, its day being the same certificate's

steps.say: FamilySearch's page of the certificate, archived under the file's citation: the death as 1946, his parents and his wife

expect.why: his name is the file's claim: the owner decides the page

steps.say: the owner accepts the page as his

expect.why: the page gives the year alone, which agrees with the file's 10th

steps.say: the certificate's image, archived under the same citation
the model reads the deceased from the image, typed by the harness from its own words: John Young Davidson, 71, died the 11th day of June 1946 at Franklin, Simpson County, state file 14205

expect.why: the image is a copy of the record the owner has decided: its reading gets no card of its own
the decision on the page's entry is the record's: the image's deceased takes it
the image's day is the certificate's own, first-hand: the rule settles the file's 10th for it

steps.say: FamilySearch's index entry of the same death, archived under the same citation as the archive holds it

expect.why: archived under the same citation: a copy of the record, decided with it

steps.say: the same death as the line of the state's own index file holds it, Reclaim the Records' copy, certificate 14205 of 1946

expect.why: the line gives the certificate's number and year, which the image's reading gives: a copy of the record, decided with it

steps.say: the screen cites the record once: the page, the image and the line are statements of the record the index entry's sha256 keys, the copy that sorts first
the written conclusion of his death: one death certificate, four copies beneath it, and the conflict the rule settled

reason.has: states the death first-hand, 11 Jun 1946 (original, primary, direct)

expect.why: one record is one source wherever it is held: cited once, its copies beneath it

steps.say: the owner's word: the line is not this record

copies.note: harness: the line is kept apart to see what the decision carried to it given back

expect.why: what the decision carried to the line is given back: its entry is a card again

why.has: the death date, which the tree holds only from the death certificate, the original this record was copied from

expect.why: kept apart, it is still the same person's record of the same death: the certificate's day is no corroboration of itself

steps.say: reconsider carries nothing across the owner's word
